title: Role of Vitamin C at 6 Months on Incidence of Complex Regional Pain Syndrome Type I in Upper Limb Surgery (CRPS-VITC)
official: Role of Vitamin C at 6 Months on Incidence of Complex Regional Pain Syndrome Type I in Upper Limb Surgery (CRPS-VITC)
summary: Main objective: The aim of the study is to demonstrate a significant reduction of CRPS 1 when taking vitamin C during the perioperative period in upper limb surgery.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. patients over 18 yo undergoing major surgery of the upper limb
2. patients able to give their consent to follow the protocol of treatment and monitoring
3. Patient with social security coverage
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patient not wishing to be part of the study, or out of condition to express consent
2. patients suffering or having already suffered from complex regional pain syndrome type 1 or type 2
3. Patient seeking follow-up outside referral centres
4. patients unable due to personal or professional mobility, to conduct post-operative follow up
5. patients undergoing surgery with nerve suture with nerve graft
6. Patient requiring two surgical procedures on the same limb
7. emergency surgery
8. children
9. patients under guardianship
10. Woman of childbearing potential without an effective contraceptive method
11. pregnant or lactating women
12. patients with hemochromatosis
13. patients with chronic kidney disease
14. patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency
15. allergy or known hypersensitivity to one of the molecules of treatment
